population: malaria cases / transmission in the study area
study_design: ecological climate-infectious disease predictive modeling study
effect_direction: climate variables were evaluated as predictors of vector-borne disease transmission
evidence_sentence: We identified clusters of malaria risk emerging in areas (1) that showed the greatest changes in Normalized Difference Vegetation Index from pre- to postflood and (2) where residents were displaced for longer periods of time and had lower access to long-lasting insecticidal nets, both of which were associated with a positive malaria rapid diagnostic test result.
source_title: Evolution of Spatial Risk of Malaria Infection After a Pragmatic Chemoprevention Program in Response to Severe Flooding in Rural Western Uganda
